none.label: Local only — nothing is deployed anywhere; `make verify` is the end of the road

aws.label: AWS — one ECS service per app deployed blue/green behind its own load balancer, RDS Postgres, Cognito and S3 + CloudFront, provisioned by OpenTofu and deployed by the trunk pipeline

azure.label: Azure — one Container App per app deployed by revision behind the environment's own ingress and managed certificate, PostgreSQL Flexible Server, Entra ID and Static Web Apps, provisioned by OpenTofu and deployed by the trunk pipeline

existing.label: Existing — this project deploys to infrastructure it does not own: whatever runs it is described in `docs/deployment.md` and provisioned by nobody here; `make verify` is the gate and nothing is deployed by the factory (experimental, with brownfield adoption)

typescript.label: TypeScript — Node and npm workspaces, ESLint, `tsc`, Vitest

java-quarkus.label: Java — Quarkus owns startup (Agroal, Flyway, SmallRye Health, OIDC); Maven, Checkstyle/PMD/SpotBugs, JUnit 5

java-spring.label: Java — Spring Boot owns startup (HikariCP, Flyway, Actuator, Spring Security); Maven, Checkstyle/PMD/SpotBugs, JUnit 5

event-store.description: Where events live. Every answer is an append-only log behind one port, and the in-memory adapter ships with all of them, so `make verify` needs no Docker whichever store is chosen

memory.label: In-memory — zero infrastructure, loses all truth on restart. The adapter the port's contract runs against in `make verify`

sqlite.label: SQLite — a real append-only log in one file, no container. Serialised writes, so it cannot prove concurrent behaviour

postgres.label: Postgres — append-only table, unique (stream, version) as the concurrency control

http.description: What accepts inbound HTTP. One transport per backend, the ecosystem's own, or none for a library or worker

none.label: None — library or worker only, no inbound HTTP

fastify.label: Fastify — JSON API, schema-parsed at the edge

fastapi.label: FastAPI — JSON API on ASGI, schema-parsed at the edge

net-http.label: net/http — standard-library JSON API, no framework dependency

quarkus-rest.label: Quarkus REST — JSON API on the framework's own HTTP layer, with SmallRye Health serving the readiness probe

spring-web.label: Spring MVC — JSON API on Tomcat over virtual threads, with Actuator serving the readiness probe

auth.description: Who authenticates staff. Every provider on this axis is an OIDC issuer and OIDC is what the adapters speak, so the protocol is the one thing every answer has in common — which is why the axis is named for the role and not for it

keycloak.label: Keycloak — self-hosted OIDC, container and group mapping scaffolded (the flow itself is NOT implemented)

cognito.label: Cognito — a user pool with the staff groups, a hosted login and a confidential client, provisioned in AWS; Keycloak runs locally as the stand-in, with the same groups and OIDC_* keys (the flow itself is NOT implemented)

entra.label: Entra ID — an app registration with the staff groups and a confidential client, provisioned in the subscription's own workforce tenant; Keycloak runs locally as the stand-in, with the same groups and OIDC_* keys (the flow itself is NOT implemented)

auth0.label: Auth0 — an application, an API and the staff roles, provisioned through Auth0's own Management API rather than by the cloud, with a post-login action putting the roles in a namespaced claim; Keycloak runs locally as the stand-in, with the same groups and OIDC_* keys (the flow itself is NOT implemented)

users.description: Who authenticates the product's own users — accounts anyone on the internet can create, with sign-up, verification, password reset and a login the browser app owns. Never the staff directory: a separate realm or tenant, even on the same vendor. Every answer is an OIDC issuer, so a service validates a customer's token the way it validates a staff one, against a different issuer

keycloak.label: Keycloak — a customers realm beside the staff realm in the same container, self-registration and password reset on, a public PKCE client for the browser app; the browser login is real, and a service's token validation is the framework's where one owns startup and NOT implemented where none does

cognito.label: Cognito — a second user pool for the product's users with self-registration and a public PKCE client, provisioned in AWS; Keycloak's customers realm runs locally as the stand-in, and the browser login is real

auth0.label: Auth0 — a database connection with self-registration and password reset, and a public PKCE client for the browser app, provisioned through Auth0's own Management API rather than by the cloud; Keycloak's customers realm is the local stand-in, and the browser login is real

codegraph.name: CodeGraph
codegraph.description: Indexes the codebase into a local knowledge graph your coding agent can query over MCP, so it can trace callers, dependencies, and the blast radius of a change across files.

uipro.name: UI/UX Pro Max
uipro.description: Installs the ui-ux-pro-max skill into skills/: an offline, searchable design-system generator (styles, palettes, type pairings, chart types and UX rules by product type) a slice consults before deciding what its screen looks like. Needs a browser app.

ux-gates.name: UX gates
ux-gates.description: Installs the ux-ui-agent-skills kit under tools/ and adds its objective gates to make verify: no literal colour, size or duration outside the design tokens, and real-render contrast, focus, target-size, responsive and axe checks over screen previews where a browser is present. Needs a browser app.

standard.label: Standard — walking skeleton, executable test and the CD gate, over state-stored persistence. The cheaper start and the irreversible one: cost compounds as one aggregate accretes every new feature, and history you never recorded cannot be recovered. For a tool, a spike, an internal script — anything whose expected lifespan is short

event-modelling.label: Event Modeling — everything above, plus events as the source of truth, built one stamped slice at a time. Cost per slice stays flat as the system grows, and folding the log back down into tables stays available. Recommended for a product a team will grow for years
